defect_origin: fork commit f1b7aebff8c2 (Federico Ficarelli 2022-08-25, [LLVM/PULP/SNITCH] Support for PULP and Snitch cores/platforms) added fixupLoopInstrs with the single-pass sizing and 'bool offsetIncrease'
root_cause: fixupLoopInstrs chose lp.setupi vs long form (and padded short loops) in one forward pass: an outer loop was sized before its inner loops got padding nops / long form, and the 4-byte alignment padding that runOnMachineFunction later puts before each moved setup was never counted. The margin of the arbitrary 50-byte limit (encoding allows 58) usually hid this; e.g. an outer lp.setupi around three padded one-instruction loops is measured 50 and ends at 68 bytes -> 'fixup value out of range'. The bool offsetIncrease (adds 1, not the byte count) is the same bookkeeping but alone never changed a decision (it only shifts blocks after the insertion, for which setup and end shift equally). Separately, loops beyond the lp.setup/lp.endi 12-bit range aborted ('UNHANDLED ...') or failed in the assembler.
fix: fixupOneLoopLength measures each loop (measureHwLoop: getInstSizeInBytes sizes, exact 4-byte alignment padding when the setup is itself 4-aligned, worst case A-G otherwise, as BranchRelaxation::postOffset), applies one change (long form or padding) and is repeated until nothing changes (BranchRelaxation.cpp:770 fixed-point). Defaults of -pulp-loop-range-immediate/-register are the encoding limits (58 / 8186 bytes from loop start to last instruction; end offset 62 / 8190), user values capped there. removeTooLongLoops (before fixupLoopLatch) deletes the setup of a loop whose conservative upper bound cannot be encoded by lp.setup / lp.endi, keeping the complete software loop (same mechanism as the existing removeUncountableLoops). The use-after-erase of MII after the long-form expansion in the old code is gone.
code_change: Only loops near a limit: (a) loops whose setupi end distance is 56-62 bytes (old limit 50 + setup 4 = 54) now keep lp.setupi instead of the 12-byte long form (GAP9 GCC also uses lp.setupi up to distance 60 in its own tests); (b) outer loops that the old code wrongly kept as lp.setupi now take the long form (near-limit set: the one base compile failure); (c) loops within a few bytes of 8190 become software loops where base still fit (conservative bound; 3 of 8 near-limit builds at N=2045-2046) and loops that base could not compile at all now compile as software loops. GAP9 sweep: byte-identical.
seed_6635: NOT fixed; different cause. -O3 (all variants) still 'fixup value out of range' with base and new. Machine block placement laid inner loop .LBB0_5 out ABOVE its preheader: 'lp.setup x0, a4, .LBB0_34; j .LBB0_5' with end label .LBB0_34 before the setup (negative offset), which no setup form can encode. The fixup pass's fixupLoopLayout/fixupLoopPreheader do not handle 'loop placed above its setup'. Kernel: logs/20-F025/seed6635.kern.c. New code skips such loops in the range logic (no negative-length arithmetic); assembler still reports it.
